name: as.Date.yearqtr
title: An Index Class for Quarterly Data

origin.description: Date at a fraction of the way through a quarter.

arguments.name: frac
arguments.text: Number from 0 to 1. Zero is the first day of the quarter and one is the last day.

origin.details: The starting month is January, April, July, or October. The last day is 100 days after the first of that month, minus the day-of-month of that later date. The result mixes the first and last days by frac and is stored as days since 1970-01-01.
origin.example:
x <- as.yearqtr(2000 + seq(0, 7)/4)
cat(paste(as.character(as.Date(x)), collapse = " "), "\n", sep = "")
cat(paste(as.character(as.Date(x, frac = 1)), collapse = " "), "\n", sep = "")

translation.description: Date at a fraction of the way through a quarter.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A Yearqtr, or the numeric values a yearqtr stores.

arguments.name: frac
arguments.text: Number from 0 to 1. Zero is the first day of the quarter and one is the last day.

translation.details: The returned RDate.days are days since 1970-01-01. Quarter 1 starts on 1 January. The last day is 100 days after that first day, minus the day-of-month of the later date, which is 31 March in both leap and non-leap years.
translation.example:
import math
import numpy as np
from zoo.yearmon import civil_from_days
from zoo.yearqtr import as_date_yearqtr, as_yearqtr
x = as_yearqtr(2000 + np.arange(8) / 4)
def iso(dates):
    parts = []
    for day in dates.days:
        y, m, d = civil_from_days(math.trunc(float(day)))
        parts.append(f"{y:04d}-{m:02d}-{d:02d}")
    return " ".join(parts)
print(iso(as_date_yearqtr(x)))
print(iso(as_date_yearqtr(x, frac=1)))
